watchtime.title: Watchtime (!watchtime)
watchtime.subtitle: How long each person has been watching the current stream

blocks.x: `!watchtime` answers in the chat how long the person who types it has been watching today's stream. The counter is per broadcast: it resets when the stream ends.
It only works on Twitch. On Kick the command answers that watch time is not available on that platform yet.

items: It counts the time of whoever writes in the chat while the channel is live.
With Count lurkers on (it is by default) it also counts people watching without writing, using the list of viewers connected to the Twitch chat. The bots in your bot list do not add time.

blocks.x: That time is also used by other modules: the "watch time" requirement and weight of Giveaways, and the Wheel and Raffle weights.

head: Option
What it does
rows: Turns the command on or off.
The command can be renamed to anything you want (for example `!tiempo`).
Seconds between uses in the whole chat, from 0 to 60 (default 5).
Seconds each person must wait, from 0 to 300 (default 30).
Minimum level to use it: everyone, subscribers, VIPs, moderators, Lead Moderators or the streamer only. Higher levels can always use it.
Also records people who do not write.
If the channel is not live it does not answer. Off by default. Before answering it checks Twitch in real time.
Adds the person's place in the ranking of the current stream (on by default).
From 0 to 30 minutes; with 0 it always answers.

blocks.x: There are four messages. The last three can be turned on or off:

items: Main message: the one sent normally. By default: "@{user} you have been watching the stream for {hours} hour(s) {minutes} minute(s)" (the default text is in Spanish; edit it to your language).
First time: if the person has not accumulated even a minute yet.
Not enough time: if they have not reached the minimum time to answer.
Stream offline: what is answered if you turned on "Only when live" and the channel is not streaming.

head: Variable
Replaced by
rows: The user who typed the command.
The hours, minutes and seconds of the accumulated time (minutes and seconds go from 0 to 59).
The place in the ranking, like #3.

public.title: Public commands page and !commands
public.subtitle: A page with your commands for people who do not know which ones exist

blocks.x: Your channel has a public page with the list of its commands, with no sign-in needed: `decatron.net/commands/your-channel`. It is meant to go in your channel's info panel or in a chat link.
In the chat, `!commands` answers with that link. It has a 10-second wait per channel.

items: The default commands you have enabled.
Your active custom commands, with their restriction.
Your micro commands and your scripts.
The Song Request commands, if that module is active.

blocks.x: Each command is shown with its name and a description; custom and Song Request commands also say who can use them.
In Commands → Public view you see your link (with a button to copy it) and the list of commands. For each one you can:

items: Hide it from the public page.
Write a public description different from the one it has.

blocks.x: Press save to publish the changes.

clip.title: Clip (!clip)
clip.subtitle: Create a clip of the live stream from chat

blocks.x: `!clip` creates a clip of what just happened on the live stream and posts the link in chat. Anyone the channel allows can type it. It is off by default: the streamer turns it on in Commands → Clip.
It only works on Twitch. Kick doesn't let a bot create clips; there the command says it isn't available or stays silent, depending on what the streamer chose.
The clip is created with the streamer's own account, so on Twitch it shows as created by them. Who asked for it is recorded in Decatron's history.

head: You type
Result
rows: A clip with the channel's default duration (30 seconds unless they changed it)
A clip with the default duration and that title

items: If the first thing you type is a number, it is read as the duration. So `!clip 2024 recap` is read as a duration of 2024 seconds and the bot says it is out of range.
The duration goes from 5 to 60 seconds, which is what Twitch allows. The streamer can narrow it further.
The title can be up to 100 characters, and Twitch checks it with AutoMod.

The bot waits for Twitch to finish creating the clip (up to 60 seconds) and then writes the link. If it takes more than 10 seconds, it says once that it is still waiting. If it isn't ready in time, it says so and you can try again.

blocks.x: The streamer picks the minimum rank. Higher ranks can always use it.

items: Everyone (default), followers, subscribers, VIPs, moderators, lead moderators or the streamer only.
For «followers» the bot asks Twitch on every use; subscribers, VIPs and moderators pass without a check.
Blocked users can't use it, whatever their rank.

head: Limit
Default
Detail
rows: Minimum time between one clip and the next, from anyone. It also applies to moderators and the streamer
Each person waits that long before creating another clip. Moderators and above skip it, unless the streamer turns that off
How many clips each person can create in a single stream

blocks.x: Cooldowns are only spent when the request passes the checks and the channel is live. They are kept in memory: if the bot restarts, they start from zero.
The bot answers with a message depending on the reason:

items: The channel isn't live: Twitch only allows clips during the stream.
The channel has clips turned off, or limited them to followers or subscribers.
The category being played doesn't allow clips.
The title didn't pass Twitch's filter.
The linked account is missing the clips permission: the streamer must link their Decatron account again.
Twitch is limiting clips right now or didn't respond; you can try again.
Duration out of range, duration or title not allowed, rank too low, blocked user, cooldown or stream limit.

blocks.x: Copyrighted music: Twitch checks the audio of clips and doesn't publish those with protected music. In that case the creation is accepted but the clip never appears and the bot says it wasn't ready in time. Twitch's own clip button blocks it too. With royalty-free music or no music it works.
It's in Commands → Clip. Anyone with permission to configure the channel can see and change it.

head: Tab
What it does
rows: Command switch, reply language (Spanish or English) and other names for the command (aliases). Minimum, default and maximum duration, and whether anyone can choose the duration. Whether a title is allowed and its length. What it does on Kick. Whether the video is also downloaded and how many days the history is kept
Minimum rank and list of blocked users
Channel cooldown, per-user cooldown, whether staff skip it, and the limit per user and stream
The 22 texts the bot writes, in Spanish and English. An empty field uses Decatron's text. Each message shows the variables it accepts
Every attempt, created or failed: who asked, with what rank, title, duration and link. You can filter it and remove records

items: Aliases are saved in lowercase and without «!», with letters, numbers and underscores, up to 10. The name `clip` always works.
While `!clip` is turned on in the channel, it answers that name before any custom command: if you already had one called `!clip`, it stops responding.
Moderators and above can choose the duration even if the channel doesn't allow it for everyone else. The title, on the other hand, is allowed or not for everybody.
By default only the link and the history are saved. No video is downloaded.

If the streamer turns on «Also download the video», every clip created is downloaded to the platform archive. If the server is low on free space, downloads pause by themselves and the link keeps being saved. The administrator can set a monthly download limit per channel.
The history is kept for 90 days by default; you can change that or keep it forever. After that time the rows are deleted automatically, but downloaded videos are not.
When you remove a record from the history, the downloaded video is only deleted if the streamer confirms it and no other record uses it.
